## js/002-boxes.js

```javascript
// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.
// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.

const Boxes = (() => {
  const BOX_W         = 180;
  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;
  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;
  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units
  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;

  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', branch: '#ff8c42', data: '#4caf7d' };

  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }
  let boxes = {};

  // {{{ box_height
  function box_height(box) {
    const n = Math.max(
      (box.inputs || []).length,
      (box.kind === 'branch' ? (box.ports || []).length : (box.outputs || []).length)
    );
    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + n * PORT_ROW_H + 8);
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ port_positions
  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.
  function port_positions(box) {
    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;
    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;
    const h  = box_height(box);
    const inputs  = box.inputs  || [];
    const outputs = box.kind === 'branch' ? (box.ports || []) : (box.outputs || []);

    const in_pts  = inputs.map((p, i) => ({
      name: p.name, side: 'input',
      x: bx,
      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,
    }));
    const out_pts = outputs.map((p, i) => ({
      name: p.name, side: 'output',
      x: bx + BOX_W,
      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,
    }));
    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ draw_box
  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {
    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;
    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;
    const w = BOX_W;
    const h = box_height(box);
    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';
    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';

    // shadow when selected
    if (selected) {
      ctx.shadowColor = color;
      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;
    }

    // body
    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';
    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';
    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);
    ctx.fill();
    ctx.stroke();

    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;

    // header bar
    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);
    ctx.fill();

    // label
    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';
    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';
    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';
    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);

    // kind badge (top right)
    ctx.fillStyle  = color;
    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';
    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';
    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);

    // port dots and labels
    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);

    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';
    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';

    in_pts.forEach((p, i) => {
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);
      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';
      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';
      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;
      ctx.fill();
      ctx.stroke();

      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';
      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';
      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);
    });

    // branch ports use palette colors
    const port_palette = ['#ff8c42','#4a9eff','#4caf7d','#e91e63','#9c27b0','#00bcd4'];
    out_pts.forEach((p, i) => {
      const dot_color = (box.kind === 'branch') ? port_palette[i % port_palette.length] : color;
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);
      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';
      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;
      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;
      ctx.fill();
      ctx.stroke();

      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';
      ctx.textAlign  = 'right';
      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);
    });
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ draw_all
  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {
    for (const id in boxes) {
      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);
    }
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ hit_test_port
  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.
  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {
    for (const id in boxes) {
      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);
      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {
        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;
        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {
          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };
        }
      }
    }
    return null;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ hit_test_box
  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.
  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {
    for (const id in boxes) {
      const b = boxes[id];
      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;
      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;
    }
    return null;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ get_port_world_pos
  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {
    const box = boxes[box_id];
    if (!box) return null;
    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);
    const list = side === 'input' ? inputs : outputs;
    const p = list.find(p => p.name === port_name);
    return p ? { x: p.x, y: p.y } : null;
  }
  // }}}

  return {
    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,
    box_height, port_positions,
    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,
  };
})();
```

## js/003-api.js

```javascript
// Thin fetch wrapper for the soramech-server REST API.
// All functions are async and throw on non-2xx responses.

const API = (() => {
  let base_url = '';
  let map_name = '';

  // {{{ init
  function init(url, name) { base_url = url.replace(/\/$/, ''); map_name = name; }
  // }}}

  // {{{ request
  async function request(method, path, body) {
    const opts = { method, headers: {} };
    if (body !== undefined) {
      opts.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';
      opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);
    }
    const res = await fetch(base_url + path, opts);
    const text = await res.text();
    let data;
    try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch { data = { error: text }; }
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`);
    return data;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ list_maps
  async function list_maps() { return request('GET', '/maps'); }
  // }}}

  // {{{ list_boxes
  async function list_boxes() {
    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes`);
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ get_box
  async function get_box(id) {
    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ put_box
  async function put_box(id, data) {
    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`, data);
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ delete_box
  async function delete_box(id) {
    return request('DELETE', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ get_meta
  async function get_meta() {
    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`);
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ put_meta
  async function put_meta(data) {
    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/meta`, data);
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ get_data
  async function get_data(filename) {
    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`);
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ put_data
  async function put_data(filename, data) {
    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/data/${filename}`, data);
  }
  // }}}

  return { init, list_maps, list_boxes, get_box, put_box, delete_box,
           get_meta, put_meta, get_data, put_data };
})();
```

## js/004-inspector.js

```javascript
// Inspector sidebar: shows and edits the selected box's fields.
// Fires PUT to the server on every field change (autosave).

const Inspector = (() => {
  const panel  = document.getElementById('inspector');
  const title  = document.getElementById('inspector-title');
  const fields = document.getElementById('inspector-fields');

  let current_box = null;
  let on_change_cb = null;

  // {{{ hide
  function hide() {
    panel.classList.add('hidden');
    current_box = null;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ save
  async function save() {
    if (!current_box) return;
    try {
      await API.put_box(current_box.id, current_box);
      if (on_change_cb) on_change_cb(current_box);
    } catch(e) {
      console.error('autosave failed:', e.message);
      status_msg('save error: ' + e.message, 'error');
    }
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ mk_row
  function mk_row(label_text, input_el) {
    const row = document.createElement('div');
    row.className = 'field-row';
    const lbl = document.createElement('label');
    lbl.textContent = label_text;
    row.appendChild(lbl);
    row.appendChild(input_el);
    return row;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ mk_text_input
  function mk_text_input(value, on_input) {
    const inp = document.createElement('input');
    inp.type  = 'text';
    inp.value = value || '';
    inp.addEventListener('input', () => { on_input(inp.value); save(); });
    return inp;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ mk_port_list
  function mk_port_list(ports, on_change) {
    const wrap = document.createElement('div');
    wrap.className = 'port-list';

    const render_ports = () => {
      wrap.innerHTML = '';
      ports.forEach((p, i) => {
        const row = document.createElement('div');
        row.className = 'port-row';

        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');
        name_inp.type  = 'text';
        name_inp.value = p.name || '';
        name_inp.placeholder = 'name';
        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });

        const type_inp = document.createElement('input');
        type_inp.type  = 'text';
        type_inp.value = p.type || '';
        type_inp.placeholder = 'type';
        type_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].type = type_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });

        const del_btn = document.createElement('button');
        del_btn.textContent = '×';
        del_btn.className   = 'port-del';
        del_btn.addEventListener('click', () => { ports.splice(i, 1); render_ports(); on_change(); save(); });

        row.appendChild(name_inp);
        row.appendChild(type_inp);
        row.appendChild(del_btn);
        wrap.appendChild(row);
      });

      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');
      add_btn.textContent = '+ port';
      add_btn.className   = 'add-port';
      add_btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        ports.push({ name: '', type: 'string' });
        render_ports();
        on_change();
        save();
      });
      wrap.appendChild(add_btn);
    };

    render_ports();
    return wrap;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ mk_branch_port_list
  function mk_branch_port_list(ports, on_change) {
    const OPS = ['eq','lt','gt','lte','gte','contains','matches'];
    const wrap = document.createElement('div');
    wrap.className = 'port-list';

    const render_ports = () => {
      wrap.innerHTML = '';
      ports.forEach((p, i) => {
        const row = document.createElement('div');
        row.className = 'port-row branch-port-row';

        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');
        name_inp.type  = 'text';
        name_inp.value = p.name || '';
        name_inp.placeholder = 'port name';
        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });
        row.appendChild(name_inp);

        if (p.name !== 'else') {
          if (!p.predicate) p.predicate = { op: 'eq', value: '' };

          const op_sel = document.createElement('select');
          OPS.forEach(op => {
            const opt = document.createElement('option');
            opt.value = op; opt.textContent = op;
            if (op === p.predicate.op) opt.selected = true;
            op_sel.appendChild(opt);
          });
          op_sel.addEventListener('change', () => { ports[i].predicate.op = op_sel.value; save(); });

          const val_inp = document.createElement('input');
          val_inp.type  = 'text';
          val_inp.value = p.predicate.value ?? '';
          val_inp.placeholder = 'value';
          val_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].predicate.value = val_inp.value; save(); });

          row.appendChild(op_sel);
          row.appendChild(val_inp);
        }

        // can't delete the else port
        if (p.name !== 'else') {
          const del_btn = document.createElement('button');
          del_btn.textContent = '×';
          del_btn.className   = 'port-del';
          del_btn.addEventListener('click', () => { ports.splice(i, 1); render_ports(); on_change(); save(); });
          row.appendChild(del_btn);
        }

        wrap.appendChild(row);
      });

      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');
      add_btn.textContent = '+ port';
      add_btn.className   = 'add-port';
      add_btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        // insert before else
        const else_i = ports.findIndex(p => p.name === 'else');
        const new_port = { name: '', predicate: { op: 'eq', value: '' } };
        if (else_i >= 0) ports.splice(else_i, 0, new_port);
        else ports.push(new_port);
        render_ports(); on_change(); save();
      });
      wrap.appendChild(add_btn);
    };

    render_ports();
    return wrap;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ show
  function show(box, on_changed) {
    current_box  = box;
    on_change_cb = on_changed;
    panel.classList.remove('hidden');
    title.textContent = box.id;
    fields.innerHTML  = '';

    fields.appendChild(mk_row('label',
      mk_text_input(box.label, v => { current_box.label = v; })));

    fields.appendChild(mk_row('kind', (() => {
      const sel = document.createElement('select');
      ['call','branch','data'].forEach(k => {
        const opt = document.createElement('option');
        opt.value = k; opt.textContent = k;
        if (k === box.kind) opt.selected = true;
        sel.appendChild(opt);
      });
      sel.addEventListener('change', () => { current_box.kind = sel.value; show(current_box, on_change_cb); save(); });
      return sel;
    })()));

    if (box.kind === 'call' || box.kind === 'data') {
      fields.appendChild(mk_row('ref',
        mk_text_input(box.ref, v => { current_box.ref = v; })));
      fields.appendChild(mk_row('fn',
        mk_text_input(box.fn, v => { current_box.fn = v; })));
    }

    const inputs_sec = document.createElement('div');
    inputs_sec.className = 'section-label';
    inputs_sec.textContent = 'inputs';
    fields.appendChild(inputs_sec);
    if (!current_box.inputs) current_box.inputs = [];
    fields.appendChild(mk_port_list(current_box.inputs, () => {}));

    if (box.kind === 'branch') {
      if (!current_box.ports) current_box.ports = [{ name: 'else' }];
      fields.appendChild(mk_row('retry limit',
        mk_text_input(String(box.retry_limit ?? 3),
          v => { current_box.retry_limit = parseInt(v) || 3; })));
      const ports_sec = document.createElement('div');
      ports_sec.className = 'section-label';
      ports_sec.textContent = 'ports (evaluated top-to-bottom)';
      fields.appendChild(ports_sec);
      fields.appendChild(mk_branch_port_list(current_box.ports, () => {}));
    } else {
      if (!current_box.outputs) current_box.outputs = [];
      const out_sec = document.createElement('div');
      out_sec.className = 'section-label';
      out_sec.textContent = 'outputs';
      fields.appendChild(out_sec);
      fields.appendChild(mk_port_list(current_box.outputs, () => {}));
    }
  }
  // }}}

  return { show, hide };
})();

## js/005-app.js

```javascript
// Top-level app: connects everything, loads the map, drives the render loop.

const App = (() => {
  let selected_id   = null;
  let drag_box_id   = null;
  let drag_offset   = { x: 0, y: 0 };
  let drawing_wire  = null;  // { from_box, from_port, from_side, cur_x, cur_y }
  let hover_port    = null;
  let status_el     = document.getElementById('status');

  // {{{ status_msg
  window.status_msg = function(msg, level = 'info') {
    status_el.textContent = msg;
    status_el.className   = 'status ' + level;
  };
  // }}}

  // {{{ load_map
  async function load_map() {
    status_msg('loading…');
    try {
      const ids = await API.list_boxes();
      const fetches = ids.map(id => API.get_box(id));
      const all = await Promise.all(fetches);
      Boxes.boxes = {};
      all.forEach(b => { Boxes.boxes[b.id] = b; });
      Canvas.mark_dirty();
      status_msg('loaded ' + ids.length + ' boxes');
    } catch(e) {
      status_msg('load error: ' + e.message, 'error');
    }
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ new_box_at
  async function new_box_at(wx, wy) {
    const id = 'box-' + Date.now().toString(36);
    const box = {
      id, label: 'New Box', kind: 'call',
      ref: '', fn: '', inputs: [], outputs: [], connections: [],
      ui: { x: Math.round(wx), y: Math.round(wy) },
    };
    try {
      await API.put_box(id, box);
      Boxes.boxes[id] = box;
      selected_id = id;
      Inspector.show(box, () => Canvas.mark_dirty());
      Canvas.mark_dirty();
    } catch(e) {
      status_msg('create error: ' + e.message, 'error');
    }
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ render
  function render() {
    if (Canvas.start_frame()) {
      const ctx = Canvas.ctx;
      Wires.draw_all(ctx, selected_id);
      Boxes.draw_all(ctx, selected_id);

      // draw in-progress wire
      if (drawing_wire) {
        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(drawing_wire.from_box, drawing_wire.from_port, 'output');
        if (src) {
          Wires.draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, drawing_wire.cur_x, drawing_wire.cur_y,
            '#6c72a0', false);
        }
      }
    }
    requestAnimationFrame(render);
  }
  // }}}

  // Mouse interaction
  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {
    if (e.button !== 0) return;
    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);
    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);

    // port hit?
    const port = Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y);
    if (port && port.side === 'output') {
      drawing_wire = { from_box: port.box_id, from_port: port.port_name,
                       cur_x: w.x, cur_y: w.y };
      return;
    }

    // box hit?
    const box_id = Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y);
    if (box_id) {
      selected_id = box_id;
      drag_box_id = box_id;
      const b = Boxes.boxes[box_id];
      drag_offset = { x: w.x - (b.ui?.x ?? 0), y: w.y - (b.ui?.y ?? 0) };
      Inspector.show(b, () => Canvas.mark_dirty());
      Canvas.mark_dirty();
      return;
    }

    // click on empty space: deselect
    selected_id = null;
    Inspector.hide();
    Canvas.mark_dirty();
  });

  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {
    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);
    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);

    if (drawing_wire) {
      drawing_wire.cur_x = w.x;
      drawing_wire.cur_y = w.y;
      Canvas.mark_dirty();
      return;
    }

    if (drag_box_id) {
      const b = Boxes.boxes[drag_box_id];
      if (b) {
        b.ui = b.ui || {};
        b.ui.x = Math.round(w.x - drag_offset.x);
        b.ui.y = Math.round(w.y - drag_offset.y);
        Canvas.mark_dirty();
      }
    }
  });

  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mouseup', async e => {
    if (e.button !== 0) return;
    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);
    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);

    if (drawing_wire) {
      const target_port = Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y);
      if (target_port && target_port.side === 'input' &&
          target_port.box_id !== drawing_wire.from_box) {
        await Wires.create_connection(
          drawing_wire.from_box, drawing_wire.from_port,
          target_port.box_id, target_port.port_name
        );
      }
      drawing_wire = null;
      Canvas.mark_dirty();
      return;
    }

    if (drag_box_id) {
      // persist position on mouseup
      const b = Boxes.boxes[drag_box_id];
      if (b) {
        try { await API.put_box(b.id, b); }
        catch(e) { status_msg('save position failed: ' + e.message, 'error'); }
      }
      drag_box_id = null;
    }
  });

  // Double-click to create box
  Canvas.el.addEventListener('dblclick', async e => {
    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);
    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);
    if (!Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) {
      await new_box_at(w.x, w.y);
    }
  });

  // Delete key: remove selected box or wire
  window.addEventListener('keydown', async e => {
    if (e.code !== 'Delete' && e.code !== 'Backspace') return;
    if (document.activeElement && document.activeElement.tagName === 'INPUT') return;

    const sel_wire = Wires.selected_wire();
    if (sel_wire) {
      await Wires.delete_connection(sel_wire);
      Canvas.mark_dirty();
      return;
    }

    if (selected_id) {
      const b = Boxes.boxes[selected_id];
      const conns = (b && b.connections || []).filter(c => c.from_box === selected_id);
      if (conns.length > 0) {
        const refs = conns.map(c => c.to_box).join(', ');
        if (!confirm(`Box "${selected_id}" has connections to: ${refs}.\nDelete anyway?`)) return;
      }
      try {
        await API.delete_box(selected_id);
        delete Boxes.boxes[selected_id];
        Inspector.hide();
        selected_id = null;
        Canvas.mark_dirty();
      } catch(e) {
        status_msg('delete error: ' + e.message, 'error');
      }
    }
  });

  // {{{ init
  async function init() {
    let server_url = localStorage.getItem('soramech_server') || '';
    let map_name   = localStorage.getItem('soramech_map')    || '';

    if (!server_url || !map_name) {
      server_url = prompt('Server URL:', 'http://localhost:7700') || 'http://localhost:7700';
      map_name   = prompt('Map name:',   'hello')                || 'hello';
      localStorage.setItem('soramech_server', server_url);
      localStorage.setItem('soramech_map',    map_name);
    }

    document.getElementById('map-label').textContent = map_name;
    API.init(server_url, map_name);
    await load_map();
    requestAnimationFrame(render);
  }
  // }}}

  window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
  return { load_map };
})();

## js/006-wires.js

```javascript
// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.
// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.

const Wires = (() => {
  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;
  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;
  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;
  const PORT_PALETTE = ['#ff8c42','#4a9eff','#4caf7d','#e91e63','#9c27b0','#00bcd4'];

  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_port, to_box, to_input }

  // {{{ selected_wire
  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }
  // }}}

  // {{{ bezier_point
  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {
    const mt = 1 - t;
    return {
      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,
      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,
    };
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ draw_bezier
  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {
    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;
    const cy0 = y0;
    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;
    const cy1 = y1;

    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);
    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);
    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;
    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;
    ctx.setLineDash(selected ? [] : []);
    ctx.stroke();
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ hit_test_wire
  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels
  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.
  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {
    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;
    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {
      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];
      for (const c of box.connections || []) {
        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;

        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_output || c.from_port, 'output');
        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,                   'input');
        if (!src || !dst) continue;

        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;
        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;

        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {
          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;
          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);
          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;
          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;
        }
      }
    }
    return null;
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ draw_all
  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {
    let branch_port_index = {};

    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {
      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];
      for (const c of box.connections || []) {
        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;

        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_output || c.from_port, 'output');
        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,                   'input');
        if (!src || !dst) continue;

        // branch boxes get per-port palette colors
        let color = '#4a6080';
        if (box.kind === 'branch') {
          const port_name = c.from_port;
          if (!branch_port_index[id]) branch_port_index[id] = {};
          if (branch_port_index[id][port_name] === undefined) {
            branch_port_index[id][port_name] = Object.keys(branch_port_index[id]).length;
          }
          color = PORT_PALETTE[branch_port_index[id][port_name] % PORT_PALETTE.length];
        }

        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&
          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&
          _selected_wire.from_output === c.from_output &&
          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&
          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;

        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);
      }
    }
  }
  // }}}

  // Handle wire selection via click
  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {
    if (e.button !== 0) return;
    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);
    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);

    // only try wire hit if no box was hit
    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }
    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;

    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);
    if (wire) {
      _selected_wire = wire;
    } else {
      _selected_wire = null;
    }
    Canvas.mark_dirty();
  });

  // {{{ create_connection
  // Fetch-before-PUT: read both boxes, add the connection record, write both.
  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_port, to_box_id, to_input) {
    try {
      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([
        API.get_box(from_box_id),
        API.get_box(to_box_id),
      ]);

      const conn = {
        from_box:    from_box_id,
        from_output: from_port,
        to_box:      to_box_id,
        to_input:    to_input,
      };

      // if source is a branch box the connection uses from_port not from_output
      const src_local = Boxes.boxes[from_box_id];
      if (src_local && src_local.kind === 'branch') {
        conn.from_port   = from_port;
        delete conn.from_output;
      }

      src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];
      dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];

      // avoid duplicates
      const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>
        c.from_box === conn.from_box &&
        (c.from_output || c.from_port) === from_port &&
        c.to_box === conn.to_box && c.to_input === conn.to_input
      );
      if (dup) return;

      src_box.connections.push(conn);
      dst_box.connections.push(conn);

      await Promise.all([
        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),
        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),
      ]);

      // update local cache
      Boxes.boxes[from_box_id] = src_box;
      Boxes.boxes[to_box_id]   = dst_box;

      status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + '.' + from_port + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);
      Canvas.mark_dirty();
    } catch(e) {
      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');
    }
  }
  // }}}

  // {{{ delete_connection
  async function delete_connection(conn) {
    try {
      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([
        API.get_box(conn.from_box),
        API.get_box(conn.to_box),
      ]);

      const match = c =>
        c.from_box === conn.from_box &&
        (c.from_output || c.from_port) === (conn.from_output || conn.from_port) &&
        c.to_box === conn.to_box && c.to_input === conn.to_input;

      src_box.connections = (src_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));
      dst_box.connections = (dst_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));

      await Promise.all([
        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),
        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),
      ]);

      Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box] = src_box;
      Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box]   = dst_box;

      _selected_wire = null;
      status_msg('deleted connection');
      Canvas.mark_dirty();
    } catch(e) {
      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');
    }
  }
  // }}}

  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,
           delete_connection, selected_wire };
})();
```

---

## Summary of what the editor currently does:

The SoraMech editor is a visual node/box editor with the following capabilities:

**Canvas & Navigation:**
- Pan via middle-mouse or Space+drag
- Zoom via scroll wheel
- Responsive canvas that resizes with window

**Boxes (Nodes):**
- Three box types: "call" (blue), "branch" (orange), "data" (green)
- Each box has configurable inputs, outputs, and metadata (label, ref, fn)
- Branch boxes have special "ports" instead of outputs, each with an operator (eq, lt, gt, lte, gte, contains, matches) and predicate value
- Double-click empty canvas to create new box at that location
- Click box to select and open inspector
- Drag selected box to move it
- Delete/Backspace key removes selected box (with confirmation if it has outgoing connections)

**Wires (Connections):**
- Click and drag from output port to input port to create connection
- Wires render as bezier curves with colors:
  - Gray for normal call/data boxes
  - Palette-colored for branch boxes (each port gets a unique color)
- Click on wire to select it
- Delete/Backspace on selected wire to remove connection

**Inspector Sidebar:**
- Shows selected box's properties
- Edit label, kind (call/branch/data), ref, fn
- Add/remove inputs and outputs with name and type
- Branch boxes show predicate operators and values with "else" port
- All changes auto-save to server via API

**API Integration:**
- Connects to a REST backend (server URL and map name via localStorage)
- All box and connection changes persist immediately
- Two buttons: "reload" (refresh boxes from server) and "switch map" (clear storage and reload)

Now I have a clear picture. Let me lay out what's broken and what's missing before proposing anything.

**Broken today (explains why boxes don't show):**

`005-app.js` does `Boxes.boxes = {}` on load — this *replaces* the module property with a new object, but `draw_all` inside the closure still reads from the *original* empty object. The boxes load from the server and go into the new object; the renderer never sees them. The fix is to mutate the existing object (clear then repopulate) instead of replacing it.

**What exists but isn't obvious:**
- Double-click empty canvas → create box
- Drag an output port dot → draw wire → release on input port
- Click wire → select it → Delete key removes it
- Inspector autosaves on every keystroke

The user can't discover any of this because there are no visible boxes to interact with.

---

**Proposed Phase 2 — "Editor you can actually use"**

Six issues in priority order:

| ID | Title | Why |
|----|-------|-----|
| 201 | Fix box rendering closure bug | Boxes are loaded but invisible — nothing else works until this is fixed |
| 202 | Fit-to-view on map load | Once boxes render, they may be off-screen at origin; fit-to-view centers them |
| 203 | Map picker panel | Typing map names into a browser prompt is painful; replace with a list from the server |
| 204 | Visible interaction hints | User has no way to know double-click creates boxes or how wiring works |
| 205 | Run button + last-run status | Show the runner output in the editor so you don't need a separate terminal |
| 206 | Entry box designation | Editor should show which box is the entry point and let you change it |

**What ref and fn do:**

- **ref** — the path to the source file, relative to the map root. E.g. `src/greet.lua`, `src/stamp.sh`. This tells the runner which file to pass to the language driver.
- **fn** — the function name within that file to call. E.g. `hello`, `write_result`. The runner passes this as the second argument to the driver.

Together they fully specify one invocation: *"run the function `hello` from `src/greet.lua` using whatever driver handles `.lua` files."*

---

**On inputs/outputs:**

You're right, and this points to a real design gap. Right now the inspector lets you type port names and types by hand — but the function already *has* a signature. The box is just a wiring point for that function. Letting the user invent port names that don't match the function is a source of errors with no feedback.

The project convention (from CLAUDE.md) already calls for a `.info.md` sidecar next to each source file listing its public functions and their inputs/outputs. `soramech-data.info.md` is an example we wrote. That file is the natural source of truth for the editor.

The revised Phase 2 plan, with 205 dropped and this folded in:

| ID | Title |
|----|-------|
| 201 | Fix box rendering closure bug |
| 202 | Fit-to-view on map load |
| 203 | Map picker panel |
| 204 | Visible interaction hints |
| 205 | ~~Run button~~ — dropped |
| 206 | Entry box designation |
| 207 | Auto-derive ports from source file manifest (ref+fn → read info.md → populate ports read-only) |

207 needs a server endpoint to read `src/*.info.md` files, and a convention for the info.md format that the editor can parse. How are you thinking about that? Should the info.md files be the mechanism, or would you prefer something else — a doc comment in the source file, a JSON sidecar, a separate schema file?

411	function M.serve(maps_root, port)
412	    local server, err = socket.bind("*", port)
413	    if not server then
414	        io.stderr:write("server: cannot bind to port " .. port .. ": " .. tostring(err) .. "\n")
415	        os.exit(1)
416	    end
417	    server:settimeout(1)  -- 1s accept timeout so we can handle signals cleanly
418	
419	    print("soramech-server listening on :" .. port .. " (maps: " .. maps_root .. ")")
420	
421	    while true do
422	        local client, cerr = server:accept()
423	        if client then
424	            client:settimeout(5)
425	            local t_start = socket.gettime()
426	
427	            local req, rerr = parse_request(client)
428	            if req then
429	                local ok_disp, derr = pcall(dispatch, client, req, maps_root)
430	                if not ok_disp then
431	                    pcall(json_err, client, "500 Internal Server Error", tostring(derr))
432	                end
433	                local elapsed = math.floor((socket.gettime() - t_start) * 1000)
434	                print(string.format("[%.0f] %s %s (%dms)",
435	                    os.time(), req.method, req.path, elapsed))
436	            else
437	                pcall(json_err, client, "400 Bad Request", tostring(rerr))
438	            end
439	
440	            client:close()
441	        end
442	        -- cerr is "timeout" on accept timeout — that's normal, keep looping
443	    end
444	end

{
  "content":"# 201 — Fix box rendering closure bug\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nBoxes load from the server (\"loaded N boxes\" appears in the status bar) but\nnothing is drawn on the canvas. {
  "content":"// Inspector sidebar: shows and edits the selected box's fields.\n// Fires PUT to the server on every field change (autosave).\n// For call boxes, ref/fn are set via the file browser; ports are read-only and derived.\n\nconst Inspector = (() => {\n  const panel  = document.getElementById('inspector');\n  const title  = document.getElementById('inspector-title');\n  const fields = document.getElementById('inspector-fields');\n\n  let current_box  = null;\n  let on_change_cb = null;\n  let browsing     = false;\n\n  // {{{ hide\n  function hide() {\n    panel.classList.add('hidden');\n    current_box = null;\n    browsing    = false;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ save\n  async function save() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(current_box.id, current_box);\n      if (on_change_cb) on_change_cb(current_box);\n    } catch(e) {\n      console.error('autosave failed:', e.message);\n      status_msg('save error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_row\n  function mk_row(label_text, input_el) {\n    const row = document.createElement('div');\n    row.className = 'field-row';\n    const lbl = document.createElement('label');\n    lbl.textContent = label_text;\n    row.appendChild(lbl);\n    row.appendChild(input_el);\n    return row;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_text_input\n  function mk_text_input(value, on_input) {\n    const inp = document.createElement('input');\n    inp.type  = 'text';\n    inp.value = value || '';\n    inp.addEventListener('input', () => { on_input(inp.value); save(); });\n    return inp;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_readonly\n  function mk_readonly(value) {\n    const el = document.createElement('div');\n    el.className   = 'field-readonly';\n    el.textContent = value || '—';\n    return el;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_port_display\n  // Read-only list of port names.\n  function mk_port_display(ports) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-display';\n    if (!ports || ports.length === 0) {\n      const empty = document.createElement('span');\n      empty.className   = 'port-display-empty';\n      empty.textContent = '(none)';\n      wrap.appendChild(empty);\n    } else {\n      ports.forEach(p => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className   = 'port-display-row';\n        row.textContent = p.name + (p.type && p.type !== 'any' ? '  :' + p.type : '');\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n    }\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_branch_port_list\n  const OPS = ['eq','lt','gt','lte','gte','contains','matches'];\n  function mk_branch_port_list(ports, on_change) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-list';\n\n    const render_ports = () => {\n      wrap.innerHTML = '';\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-row branch-port-row';\n\n        const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n        name_inp.type  = 'text';\n        name_inp.value = p.name || '';\n        name_inp.placeholder = 'port name';\n        name_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].name = name_inp.value; on_change(); save(); });\n        row.appendChild(name_inp);\n\n        if (p.name !== 'else') {\n          if (!p.predicate) p.predicate = { op: 'eq', value: '' };\n\n          const op_sel = document.createElement('select');\n          OPS.forEach(op => {\n            const opt = document.createElement('option');\n            opt.value = op; opt.textContent = op;\n            if (op === p.predicate.op) opt.selected = true;\n            op_sel.appendChild(opt);\n          });\n          op_sel.addEventListener('change', () => { ports[i].predicate.op = op_sel.value; save(); });\n\n          const val_inp = document.createElement('input');\n          val_inp.type  = 'text';\n          val_inp.value = p.predicate.value ?? '';\n          val_inp.placeholder = 'value';\n          val_inp.addEventListener('input', () => { ports[i].predicate.value = val_inp.value; save(); });\n\n          row.appendChild(op_sel);\n          row.appendChild(val_inp);\n        }\n\n        if (p.name !== 'else') {\n          const del_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          del_btn.textContent = '×';\n          del_btn.className   = 'port-del';\n          del_btn.addEventListener('click', () => { ports.splice(i, 1); render_ports(); on_change(); save(); });\n          row.appendChild(del_btn);\n        }\n\n        wrap.appendChild(row);\n      });\n\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ port';\n      add_btn.className   = 'add-port';\n      add_btn.addEventListener('click', () => {\n        const else_i = ports.findIndex(p => p.name === 'else');\n        const new_port = { name: '', predicate: { op: 'eq', value: '' } };\n        if (else_i >= 0) ports.splice(else_i, 0, new_port);\n        else ports.push(new_port);\n        render_ports(); on_change(); save();\n      });\n      wrap.appendChild(add_btn);\n    };\n\n    render_ports();\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ open_browser\n  // Replaces inspector content with the file browser; restores on function select.\n  function open_browser() {\n    browsing = true;\n    title.textContent = 'browse src/';\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n\n    FileBrowser.render(fields, (filename, fn) => {\n      // fn = { name, inputs: [string], outputs: [string] }\n      browsing = false;\n      current_box.ref     = filename;\n      current_box.fn      = fn.name;\n      current_box.inputs  = fn.inputs.map(n  => ({ name: n,  type: 'any' }));\n      current_box.outputs = fn.outputs.map(n => ({ name: n, type: 'any' }));\n      save().then(() => show(current_box, on_change_cb));\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show\n  function show(box, on_changed) {\n    current_box  = box;\n    on_change_cb = on_changed;\n    browsing     = false;\n    panel.classList.remove('hidden');\n    title.textContent = box.id;\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('label',\n      mk_text_input(box.label, v => { current_box.label = v; })));\n\n    fields.appendChild(mk_row('kind', (() => {\n      const sel = document.createElement('select');\n      ['call','branch','data'].forEach(k => {\n        const opt = document.createElement('option');\n        opt.value = k; opt.textContent = k;\n        if (k === box.kind) opt.selected = true;\n        sel.appendChild(opt);\n      });\n      sel.addEventListener('change', () => { current_box.kind = sel.value; show(current_box, on_change_cb); save(); });\n      return sel;\n    })()));\n\n    if (box.kind === 'call' || box.kind === 'data') {\n      // ref: display + browse button in one row\n      const ref_wrap = document.createElement('div');\n      ref_wrap.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:4px;align-items:center;';\n      const ref_disp = document.createElement('div');\n      ref_disp.className   = 'field-readonly';\n      ref_disp.style.flex  = '1';\n      ref_disp.textContent = box.ref || '—';\n      const browse_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      browse_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n      browse_btn.textContent = 'browse';\n      browse_btn.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap';\n      browse_btn.onclick = open_browser;\n      ref_wrap.appendChild(ref_disp);\n      ref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('ref', ref_wrap));\n\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('fn', mk_readonly(box.fn)));\n\n      const in_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      in_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      in_sec.textContent = 'inputs';\n      fields.appendChild(in_sec);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_port_display(box.inputs));\n\n      const out_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      out_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      out_sec.textContent = 'outputs';\n      fields.appendChild(out_sec);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_port_display(box.outputs));\n    }\n\n    if (box.kind === 'branch') {\n      if (!current_box.ports) current_box.ports = [{ name: 'else' }];\n      fields.appendChild(mk_row('retry limit',\n        mk_text_input(String(box.retry_limit ?? 3),\n          v => { current_box.retry_limit = parseInt(v) || 3; })));\n\n      // branch inputs are still manually configured (no source function to parse)\n      const in_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      in_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      in_sec.textContent = 'inputs';\n      fields.appendChild(in_sec);\n      if (!current_box.inputs) current_box.inputs = [];\n      const in_list = document.createElement('div');\n      in_list.className = 'port-list';\n      (current_box.inputs || []).forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-row';\n        const ni = document.createElement('input');\n        ni.type = 'text'; ni.value = p.name || ''; ni.placeholder = 'name';\n        ni.addEventListener('input', () => { current_box.inputs[i].name = ni.value; save(); });\n        const ti = document.createElement('input');\n        ti.type = 'text'; row.appendChild(del);\n        in_list.appendChild(row);\n      });\n      const add_in = document.createElement('button');\n      add_in.textContent = '+ input'; add_in.className = 'add-port';\n      add_in.addEventListener('click', () => {\n        current_box.inputs.push({ name: '', type: 'any' });\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb); save();\n      });\n      in_list.appendChild(add_in);\n      fields.appendChild(in_list);\n\n      const ports_sec = document.createElement('div');\n      ports_sec.className   = 'section-label';\n      ports_sec.textContent = 'ports (evaluated top-to-bottom)';\n      fields.appendChild(ports_sec);\n      fields.appendChild(mk_branch_port_list(current_box.ports, () => {}));\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { show, hide };\n})();\n",

The north star use case is LLM orchestration.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Map directory format: `boxes/<id>.json`, `data/*.json`, `drivers.json`, `meta.json`, `tmp/` symlink
   - Connection format: 4-field record `{from_box, from_output OR from_port, to_box, to_input}` stored identically in BOTH endpoint box files
   - Language driver contract: `<driver> <file> <fn> <arg_count> [args...]` → JSON array on stdout where each element is itself a JSON-encoded value
   - SORAMECH_MAP_DIR global injected by lua driver shim so box functions can locate data files
   - Branch boxes: `kind: "branch"`, named output `ports` with predicates (eq/lt/gt/lte/gte/contains/matches), always have "else" port
   - Data file format: `{constant: bool, fields: {key: {constant: bool, value: any}}}`
   - Atomic writes: write to `.tmp` then `os.rename`
   - JS module pattern (IIFE): all editor modules use `const Mod = (() => { ... return {...}; })();`
   - Closure reference bug: reassigning `Boxes.boxes = {}` breaks the closure; must mutate the existing object instead
   - Server routes use a dispatch table pattern matching method + path parts array
   - File browser parses Lua (`function M.name(args)` + return statement scanning) and Bash (`name() {` + `local var="${N}"` scanning)

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`src/001-schema.lua`**
     - Added `validate_incoming_connection` function accepting either `from_output` or `from_port`
     - Changed `validate_box` to route by direction: `if c.from_box == box.id` → kind-specific validator, else → incoming validator
     ```lua
     local function validate_incoming_connection(c, i, errors)
         if c.from_box == nil then err(errors, "connection[" .. i .. "] missing 'from_box'") end
         if c.from_output == nil and c.from_port == nil then
             err(errors, "connection[" .. i .. "] missing both 'from_output' and 'from_port'")
         end
         if c.to_box == nil then err(errors, "connection[" .. i .. "] missing 'to_box'") end
         if c.to_input == nil then err(errors, "connection[" .. i .. "] missing 'to_input'") end
     end
     ```

   - **`libs/soramech-data.lua`**

     - Atomic writes via write-to-.tmp-then-os.rename

   - **`tests/003-data-test.lua`**

-- Hello function for the hello example map.
-- Reads the name from data/state.json and returns a greeting string.
-- No inputs: name comes from the map's data file at runtime.

local json = require("dkjson")
local M    = {}

-- {{{ read_name
local function read_name(map_dir)
    -- walk up from this file's location to find the map root's data/state.json
    local state_path = map_dir .. "/data/state.json"
    local f = io.open(state_path, "r")
    if not f then return "world" end
    local raw  = f:read("*a")
    f:close()
    local obj, _, _ = json.decode(raw)
    if not obj then return "world" end
    local name_field = obj.fields and obj.fields.name
    if not name_field then return "world" end
    return name_field.value or "world"
```

-- Hello function for the hello example map.
-- Reads the name from data/state.json and returns a greeting string.
-- No inputs: name comes from the map's data file at runtime.

local json = require("dkjson")
local M    = {}

-- {{{ read_name
local function read_name(map_dir)
    -- walk up from this file's location to find the map root's data/state.json
    local state_path = map_dir .. "/data/state.json"
    local f = io.open(state_path, "r")
    if not f then return "world" end
    local raw  = f:read("*a")
    f:close()
    local obj, _, _ = json.decode(raw)
    if not obj then return "world" end
    local name_field = obj.fields and obj.fields.name
    if not name_field then return "world" end
    return name_field.value or "world"
end
-- }}}

-- {{{ hello
function M.hello()
    -- SORAMECH_MAP_DIR is injected by the lua driver shim at invocation time
    local name = read_name(SORAMECH_MAP_DIR or ".")
    return "Hello, " .. tostring(name) .. "!"
end
-- }}}

return M

**On per-box values:** you're right that parsing variable definitions from arbitrary downloaded libraries is a non-starter. Two approaches worth considering:

**Option A — Manual "config" table on the box.** Add a `box.config` field (key-value pairs, editable in the inspector). At runtime the runner injects them as a Lua global table before calling the function, or passes them as an extra argument. Works with any library, zero source parsing needed. The user decides which knobs exist.

**Option B — Use the existing data/ system.** Each box can already read from `data/*.json` files at runtime via `SORAMECH_MAP_DIR`. The inspector could just show a "linked data file" picker. Less editor overhead, already implemented.

My recommendation is **Option A** — a lightweight `box.config` section in the inspector (a simple add/remove key-value list, same pattern as the branch ports UI). It's self-contained per box, visible at a glance, and doesn't require the user to know the data/ directory layout. The runner side just needs one extra injected global before the function call.

ts: 2026-05-08T00:58:07.870Z

Good call — narrowing scope to your actual use case is the right move.

Here's the convention I'd propose for Lua:

```lua
function M.classify(text)
  local values = {
    keyword        = "SoraMech",
    case_sensitive = false,
    max_retries    = 3,
  }
  -- rest of function uses values.keyword, etc.
  return result
end
```

The parser already scans the function body — it just needs to also look for `local values = {` and extract the key/default-value pairs. The inspector shows them as editable fields. The box stores overrides in `box.values`. At runtime, the Lua driver sets a `SORAMECH_VALUES` global with the box's overrides before calling the function, and you write:

```lua
local values = SORAMECH_VALUES or {
  keyword = "SoraMech",
  ...
}
```

Or we add a one-liner helper to `libs/soramech-data.lua` so you don't write that every time:

```lua
local values = sora.values({ keyword = "SoraMech", ... })
-- (merges SORAMECH_VALUES overrides on top of your defaults)
```

For **C** it's harder since it's compiled. The natural approach there is: the C function reads a config file from `SORAMECH_MAP_DIR/tmp/<box_id>_values.json` that the runner writes before invoking it. Slightly more boilerplate, but the pattern is the same.

My honest take: this is a solid convention. It's readable, self-documenting, and the defaults live right next to the code that uses them. The one thing to decide before building it is the variable name — `values` vs `config` vs `params`. I'd lean toward `config` since `values` is a common local variable name that might collide accidentally.

Should I start with the parser side (extract `local config = {` blocks in the file browser) or the runner injection side first?

144	        if store[box.id .. "." .. port.name] == nil then
145	            return false
146	        end
147	    end
148	    return true
149	end
150	-- }}}
151	
152	-- {{{ collect_inputs
153	local function collect_inputs(box, store)
154	    local inputs = {}
155	    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do
156	        inputs[port.name] = store[box.id .. "." .. port.name]
157	    end
158	    return inputs
159	end
160	-- }}}
161	
162	-- {{{ fire_connections
163	local function fire_connections(box, outputs, store, queue, boxes, retry_counts)
164	    -- for branch boxes: evaluate predicates and fire the first matching port
165	    -- for call boxes: push all wired output values directly
166	    if box.kind == "branch" then
167	        local input_val = outputs["_branch_input"]
168	        local fired = false
169	        for _, port in ipairs(box.ports or {}) do
170	            if port.name == "else" then goto next_port end
171	            if port.predicate and eval_predicate(port.predicate, input_val) then
172	                -- find and fire connections from this port
173	                for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do
174	                    if c.from_box == box.id and c.from_port == port.name then
175	                        store[c.to_box .. "." .. c.to_input] = input_val
176	                        queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box
177	                    end
178	                end
179	                fired = true
180	                break
181	            end
182	            ::next_port::
183	        end
184	
185	        if not fired then
186	            -- fire "else" port
187	            for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do
188	                if c.from_box == box.id and c.from_port == "else" then
189	                    store[c.to_box .. "." .. c.to_input] = input_val
190	                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box
191	                    fired = true
192	                end
193	            end
194	
195	            if not fired then
196	                -- unwired else: return signal to re-queue the upstream box
197	                return "retry"
198	            end
199	        end
200	
201	    else
202	        -- call box: push each output value to connected input ports
203	        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do
204	            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_conn end
205	            local val = outputs[c.from_output]
206	            store[c.to_box .. "." .. c.to_input] = val
207	            -- enqueue target if all its inputs are now satisfied
208	            local target = boxes[c.to_box]
209	            if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then
210	                queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box
211	            end
212	            ::next_conn::
213	        end
214	    end
215	end
216	-- }}}
217	
218	-- {{{ write_last_run
219	local function write_last_run(map_dir, run_state)
220	    local tmp_dir = map_dir .. "/tmp"
221	    local path    = tmp_dir .. "/last-run.json"
222	    local f, ferr = io.open(path, "w")
223	    if not f then
224	        io.stderr:write("executor: cannot write last-run.json: " .. tostring(ferr) .. "\n")
225	        return
226	    end
227	    f:write(json.encode(run_state, { indent = true }))
228	    f:close()
229	end
230	-- }}}
231	
232	-- {{{ execute
233	function M.execute(graph, map_dir)
234	    local boxes    = graph.boxes
235	    local drivers  = graph.drivers
236	    local entry_id = graph.entry
237	
238	    -- store: keyed by "box_id.port_name" -> value
239	    local store = {}
240	
241	    -- per-box retry counters (for branch box else-retry)
242	    local retry_counts = {}
243	
244	    -- seed entry box: if it has inputs, they must come from data files;
245	    -- for v1, entry boxes with inputs are the user's responsibility to pre-seed
246	    -- via a data box or by starting with a box that has no inputs
247	    local entry_box = boxes[entry_id]
248	    if entry_box and #(entry_box.inputs or {}) == 0 then
249	        -- no inputs needed; ready immediately
250	    end
251	
252	    local queue   = { entry_id }
253	    local visited = {}  -- boxes that have been run (prevent double-execution)
254	    local run_log = {}  -- per-box execution records for last-run.json
255	    local map_ok  = true
256	    local map_err = nil
257	
258	    while #queue > 0 do
259	        -- dequeue
260	        local id = table.remove(queue, 1)
261	
262	        local box = boxes[id]
263	        if not box then
264	            map_ok  = false
265	            map_err = "unknown box in queue: '" .. id .. "'"
266	            break
267	        end
268	
269	        -- skip boxes whose inputs are not yet satisfied (they'll be re-enqueued)
270	        if not inputs_satisfied(box, store) then
271	            goto next_iter
272	        end
273	
274	        if visited[id] and box.kind ~= "branch" then
275	            goto next_iter
276	        end
277	        visited[id] = true
278	
279	        local inputs = collect_inputs(box, store)
280	
281	        -- branch box is handled specially: it doesn't invoke a driver,
282	        -- it routes based on its single input value
283	        local outputs, task_err
284	        if box.kind == "branch" then
285	            -- the branch input is the value wired to its single input port
286	            local branch_val = inputs[(box.inputs or {})[1] and box.inputs[1].name or "value"]
287	            outputs = { _branch_input = branch_val }
288	            task_err = nil
289	        else
290	            outputs, task_err = run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)
291	        end
292	
293	        run_log[id] = {
294	            inputs  = inputs,
295	            outputs = outputs or {},
296	            status  = task_err and "error" or "ok",
297	            error   = task_err,
298	        }
299	
300	        if task_err then
301	            map_ok  = false
302	            map_err = task_err
303	            io.stderr:write("executor: " .. task_err .. "\n")
304	            break
305	        end
306	
307	        -- fire connections and enqueue newly-ready boxes
308	        local signal = fire_connections(box, outputs, store, queue, boxes, retry_counts)
309	        if signal == "retry" then
310	            local max_retries = box.retry_limit or 3
311	            retry_counts[id] = (retry_counts[id] or 0) + 1
312	            if retry_counts[id] > max_retries then
313	                map_ok  = false
314	                map_err = "branch box '" .. id .. "' exceeded retry limit (" ..
315	                    max_retries .. ")"
316	                break
317	            end
318	            -- find the upstream box(es) that feed this branch box and re-queue them
319	            for src_id, src_box in pairs(boxes) do
320	                for _, c in ipairs(src_box.connections or {}) do
321	                    if c.from_box ~= src_id then goto next_src_conn end
322	                    if c.to_box ~= id then goto next_src_conn end
323	
324	                    visited[src_id] = nil
325	
326	                    -- clear the branch box's input from the store so it
327	                    -- re-fills when the upstream box runs again
328	                    for _, p in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do
329	                        store[id .. "." .. p.name] = nil
330	                    end
331	
332	                    -- apply retry_vary: randomize specified input fields on the
333	                    -- upstream box before re-running it
334	                    local vary = src_box.retry_vary
335	                    if vary then
336	                        for field_name, range in pairs(vary) do
337	                            local lo = tonumber(range.min) or 0
338	                            local hi = tonumber(range.max) or 1
339	                            local val = lo + math.random() * (hi - lo)
340	                            store[src_id .. "." .. field_name] = val
341	                        end
342	                    end
343	
344	                    queue[#queue + 1] = src_id
345	                    ::next_src_conn::
346	                end
347	            end
348	        end
349	
350	        ::next_iter::
351	    end
352	
353	    -- write last-run snapshot to tmp/
354	    write_last_run(map_dir, {
355	        ok     = map_ok,
356	        error  = map_err,
357	        boxes  = run_log,
358	    })
359	
360	    return map_ok, map_err
361	end
362	-- }}}
363	
364	return M
365

  "content":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\nis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\nskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\nthe editor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach input port has an optional literal value editable directly in the inspector\npanel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is connected to that port,\nthe literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS connected, the wire's value\noverwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n\nThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\nobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\nif that fails, the raw string is used.\n\nThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\ndedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Data model** — port objects in `box.inputs` gain an optional `value`\n   string field. ### [1399] type=assistant
ts: 2026-05-08T01:05:08.093Z

`src/004-executor.lua` is the runtime engine for SoraMech — the thing that actually *runs* a map you've built in the editor.

When you invoke `soramech-runner.lua` on a map, the executor:

1. **Loads the graph** — reads all the box JSON files, the connections between them, and the driver table
2. **Pre-seeds the store** — a flat key-value table keyed by `"box_id.port_name"`. Literal values you set in the inspector get written here before anything runs
3. **Starts at the entry box** — whichever box is flagged as the entry point, it gets queued first
4. **Works through the queue** — for each box:
   - Checks whether all its input ports have values in the store (`inputs_satisfied`)
   - If yes: calls the appropriate language driver (lua, bash, etc.), gets back the output values
   - Pushes those outputs into the store under the target box's input keys
   - Enqueues any downstream boxes that are now fully satisfied
5. **Branch boxes** are special — they don't call a driver, they just look at their single input value and route it to the matching output port based on predicates (eq, contains, etc.)

So in terms of dataflow: the store is the "wire memory." A wired connection writes a value into `"to_box.to_port"` at runtime. A literal value pre-writes into `"box_id.port_name"` before the loop. If a wire later fires to the same key, it overwrites it — wires win.

The executor is currently synchronous (one box at a time, in queue order). The comment at the top of `run_task` marks it as the future thread pool swap point — when multiple boxes are independently ready, they'd be handed off to worker threads instead of run in sequence.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lua/LuaJIT language driver for SoraMech.
# Loads a .lua module, calls the named function with JSON-decoded arguments,
# and writes the return value(s) as a JSON array to stdout.
# Contract: <script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]

DIR="/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech"

FILE_PATH="${1}"
FN_NAME="${2}"
ARG_COUNT="${3}"
shift 3

if [ -z "${FILE_PATH}" ] || [ -z "${FN_NAME}" ]; then
    echo "lua.sh: missing file-path or fn-name" >&2
    exit 1
fi

if ! command -v luajit > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "lua.sh: luajit not found on PATH" >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [ ! -f "${FILE_PATH}" ]; then
    echo "lua.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# build a JSON array of the raw argument strings for passing into lua
ARGS_JSON="["
SEP=""
for ARG in "$@"; do
    ARGS_JSON="${ARGS_JSON}${SEP}${ARG}"
    SEP=","
done
ARGS_JSON="${ARGS_JSON}]"

# set LUA_PATH so dkjson is findable before the shim runs its first require
export LUA_PATH="${DIR}/libs/?.lua;${LUA_PATH:-;}"

# run luajit with the driver shim inline; the shim loads the module,
# decodes arguments, calls the function, and encodes the result
luajit - "${FILE_PATH}" "${FN_NAME}" "${ARGS_JSON}" << 'LUASHIM'
local json = require("dkjson")

-- read driver arguments
local file_path = arg[1]
local fn_name   = arg[2]
local args_raw  = arg[3]

-- add libs and the module's own directory to the path for any further requires
local script_dir = file_path:match("^(.+)/[^/]+$") or "."
package.path = script_dir .. "/?.lua;" ..
               "/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/?.lua;" ..
               package.path

-- expose map root as a global so box functions can access data files without
-- needing it wired as an explicit input; convention: src/ is one level below root
SORAMECH_MAP_DIR = script_dir:match("^(.+)/[^/]+$") or script_dir

-- decode args array
local args_table, _, jerr = json.decode(args_raw)
if not args_table then
    io.stderr:write("lua.sh: failed to decode args JSON: " .. tostring(jerr) .. "\n")
    os.exit(1)
end

-- load the module
local ok, mod = pcall(dofile, file_path)
if not ok then
    io.stderr:write("lua.sh: error loading " .. file_path .. ": " .. tostring(mod) .. "\n")
    os.exit(1)
end

-- resolve the function
local fn = mod[fn_name]
if type(fn) ~= "function" then
    io.stderr:write("lua.sh: no public function '" .. fn_name .. "' in " .. file_path .. "\n")
    os.exit(1)
end

-- decode each arg from JSON to lua value; strings are passed as-is
local call_args = {}
for i, raw_arg in ipairs(args_table) do
    local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw_arg)
    if aerr then
        -- not valid JSON — treat as a plain string
        call_args[i] = raw_arg
    else
        call_args[i] = val
    end
end

-- call the function; collect all return values into a table
local results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))

-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)
local encoded = {}
for i = 1, results.n do
    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])
end
print(json.encode(encoded))
LUASHIM
```

Done. To use it in a map:

```
cp /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/ollama.lua maps/<your-map>/src/ollama.lua
```

Then in the editor: create a call box, hit browse, pick `ollama.lua`, choose `query` or `chat`. The file browser will auto-populate the ports:

- **`query`** — inputs: `prompt, model, host` → output: `result`
- **`chat`** — inputs: `prompt, system, model, host` → output: `result`

Wire `prompt` from an upstream box. Set `model`, `host`, and `system` as **literal port values** in the inspector (leave them blank to use the defaults: `llama3.2` + `localhost:11434`). That's it — no wrapper, no extra config.

If you want to call it from another Lua function instead: `local ollama = require("ollama")` works anywhere since `libs/` is already on the driver's package path.

### [1527] type=assistant
ts: 2026-05-08T01:24:27.110Z

The `ollama.lua` call box and the `llm-route` box solve different problems, and the executor treats them very differently.

**`call` box using `ollama.lua`:**

The executor doesn't know or care that it's talking to Ollama. It just sees a box with `kind: "call"`, looks up the driver (`drivers/lua.sh`), spawns a subprocess, passes the inputs as JSON arguments, and collects the return values as named output ports. The Lua function does the HTTP call internally. The executor's job is done after the function returns — it pushes the output values into the store and enqueues whatever downstream boxes are now satisfied.

**`llm-route` box:**

The executor handles it directly in `fire_connections` without spawning any subprocess. There's no driver involved. Instead, when the box runs, `llm_route_call()` in the executor itself calls `require("ollama")` and makes the Ollama request inline in Lua. The result isn't an output value pushed to downstream ports — it's a **routing decision**. The executor looks at which output port name matches the LLM's reply, then fires only that port's wire, passing the original `text` input through as the value. The other ports stay silent.

So the key difference is **data flow vs. control flow**:

- `call` box: produces output values, all wired outputs fire, downstream boxes receive data
- `llm-route` box: produces no data of its own, exactly one output wire fires, that wire carries the input text through — the box is a switch, not a transformer

It's the same distinction as between a `call` box and a `branch` box. In fact `llm-route` is implemented almost identically to `branch` in the executor — the only difference is that `branch` evaluates a hard-coded predicate (eq, contains, etc.) while `llm-route` asks Ollama to make the judgment call.

It's hard-coded into all three system layers — which is the same situation as `branch`.

**In the executor** (`004-executor.lua`): `llm_route_call()` lives there, and there are two explicit `elseif box.kind == "llm-route"` checks — one in the main execution loop, one in `fire_connections`. Touch the executor to add or change it.

**In the wires** (`006-wires.js`): two more explicit checks — one to use `from_port` instead of `from_output` when drawing a wire from it, one for the colored-wire logic.

So it's spread across three files and none of it is swappable. Compare that to `ollama.lua`, which is entirely standalone — delete the file and nothing in the system breaks.

The root issue is that **control flow can't live in a user function**. A `call` box always fires all its output wires after the function returns — the executor doesn't give the function any way to say "only fire this one port." So any box that needs to choose between output paths has to be a special kind that the executor knows about, which means it ends up baked in.

One way to fix this: give functions a way to return a *route signal* — a special return value that the executor interprets as "fire this named port with this value." Then `llm-route` could just be a Lua function in `libs/` that returns `{ _route = "positive", _value = text }`, and the executor would handle it generically for any call box that returns that shape. No new kind, no changes to the inspector or wires.

Worth considering before adding more special kinds.

The second example is the revealing one. Let me think through it:

```
function do_other_thing(d, e, f)
  if d == 2 then return (e, f)
  else return d
```

The system has to know: when two values come back, do they go to ports 1 and 2 positionally? Or to specific named ports? And when one value comes back, which port does it go to — the first one, or the one named `d`?

The current executor maps returns strictly by position: first return value → first output port, second → second, and so on. So there's actually a partial solution already baked in — if a function returns `nil` for a position, the executor skips writing that key to the store, which means the downstream box never becomes satisfied and its wire effectively doesn't fire. But to use it you'd have to write `return nil, e, f` or `return d, nil, nil` and know the port order by heart, which is fragile.

The cleaner fix is a thin routing wrapper in the standard library:

```lua
local sora = require("soramech")

function do_other_thing(d, e, f)
  if d == 2 then return sora.routes({ e_out = e, f_out = f })
  else return sora.route("d_out", d)
end
```

`sora.route` and `sora.routes` just return a specially-marked table — `{ __soramech_route = true, port = "d_out", value = d }`. The driver detects that marker and outputs a different JSON shape. The executor detects it in `fire_connections` and fires only the named ports instead of doing positional mapping.

The payoff: `llm-route` becomes a regular Lua function in `libs/` that calls Ollama and returns `sora.route(matched_port, text)`. The special kind disappears from the executor, inspector, and wires entirely — replaced by a library call any function can use.

Want me to implement that?

It solves the naming problem but not the routing problem — let me separate them.

**Routing:** The executor still gets positional return values. When the function does `return c`, the runtime value of `c` arrives at position 1 — the executor doesn't know it was called `c`. So `return c` fires the first output port, not the port *named* `c`.

The nil convention handles this, but requires the user to be explicit:

```lua
function do_thing(a, b, c)
  -- output ports in order: a, b, c
  if a < b    then return nil, nil, c    -- c fires
  if a == b   then return nil, b,   nil  -- b fires
  else             return false, nil, nil -- a fires
end
```

Since the port names are inherited and shown in order in the inspector, the user knows `c` is position 3. Returning `nil` at a position means that port's wire doesn't fire. That's already close to working in the executor — `nil` in the store means `inputs_satisfied` returns false downstream.

So the full picture is:

- Remove renaming from the inspector → ports are always what the function says they are
- Commit to a defined port order (order they appear in returns, as the parser already extracts them)
- `nil` at a position = that port doesn't fire
- The `sora.route` library is still useful for *named* routing without caring about position, but it's optional

The mutation case isn't really a system problem — it's a code readability problem. The port is correctly named `b`; the user just has to read their own function to know `b` might be 2. That's true of any programming tool. The system can't and shouldn't try to track value provenance through mutations.

The parsing approach is sound. But it still doesn't tell the executor which return value maps to which port at runtime. `return a, b, c` gives the driver three anonymous positional values — the names are lost.

The way to fix both problems at once: **require functions to return a table with named keys.**

```lua
function blahblahblah(a, b, c)
  if a == 2 then b = 2 end
  return { a = a, b = b, c = c }
end

function classify(text)
  if score > 0.5 then return { positive = text }
  else                return { negative = text }
  end
end
```

The parser reads table keys from return statements — that's already closer to what it does. The driver detects that the return value is a table (not an array) and uses it as a named map. The executor fires only the ports whose keys appear in the returned table. No positional mapping, no library wrapper, no fragility.

The mutation case looks like `{ b = b }` — the key is the port name, the value is whatever b is at that moment. That's honest and accurate.

Constants come out naturally too: `return { version = "1.0" }` — the inspector sees `"1.0"` and marks the port as constant. Complex expressions: `return { result = foo(x) }` — shows `foo(x)` verbatim, which is ugly but accurate.

The one cost: functions need to always return a table. That's a convention the user has to follow, but it's a small one and it buys complete decoupling from positional ordering.

Worth adopting?

The multi-section display idea is genuinely good for the inspector — each return statement becomes its own port group, and you can wire from whichever group you expect to fire. That's a clean UI.

The runtime problem is still there though. The driver just sees raw positional values — by the time they cross the function boundary, the names are gone. It gets back `[1, 2, 1]` and has no way to know whether that came from `return a, b, c` or `return c, b, a`. Both produce the same array.

The one case where disambiguation works automatically: when different return paths produce **different numbers of values**. If path 1 returns 3 values and path 2 returns 1, the driver can check the count and know which path fired. That covers a lot of practical cases:

```lua
function thing(a, b, c)
  if a == 2 then return a, b, c   -- 3 values → path 1
  else return c                   -- 1 value  → path 2
end
```

But your example — two paths both returning 3 values — is unresolvable without some form of tagging. The driver genuinely cannot tell them apart.

So the honest picture is:

- Different value counts → works, no idiom needed, just count-based disambiguation
- Same value counts, different variable order → unsolvable at runtime without tagging

For that second case, you're stuck choosing between: source instrumentation (fragile, complex), a tagging convention, or accepting that port names are approximate/informational when paths have equal lengths.

Maybe the pragmatic answer is: implement count-based disambiguation, show the multi-section display in the inspector, and document that "same-length ambiguous paths" are a known limitation. In practice most routing functions return different amounts from different paths anyway.
